title: Coordination, Review & Sign-Off
purpose: Define TIVERIT supplementary coordination governance within collaborative information production. S5 coordination evidence supports, but does not replace, the ISO 19650 review/approval-for-sharing and information-model delivery decisions governed through S3 and S7.

requirements.statement: Coordination activities shall be organized around distinct coordination stages or gates aligned to delivery milestones defined under S2 and shall operate as supplementary controls within collaborative information production.
All models subject to coordination shall be federated in a common, verified coordinate system before coordination checks are performed.
Coordination checks shall use defined check types, priorities, and tolerances documented in the project ruleset.
Coordination issues shall be uniquely identified, classified by priority and type, assigned to an identifiable responsible party, and tracked through a governed status progression.

A TIVERIT coordination sign-off shall be recorded at each governed coordination gate where the project requires such a gate; this sign-off records completion of the defined coordination review and is not an ISO 19650 approval-for-sharing, authorization, or acceptance decision unless the applicable project governance explicitly assigns the same authorized party and combines the decisions.

The Project BIM Manager, or delegated role per project RACI, may hold TIVERIT coordination-sign-off authority where assigned by project governance. This enterprise coordination assignment shall not be interpreted as assigning ISO 19650 task-team approval-for-sharing, lead-appointed-party authorization, or appointing-party acceptance authority.
Coordination check results, issue logs, verification results and sign-off records shall be maintained as auditable evidence and may support the applicable ISO 19650 review activity.

Unresolved coordination issues that cannot be resolved within the coordination cycle shall follow a defined escalation route and shall be visible to any subsequent review or exchange decision for which they are material.

A finding shall be treated as a governed coordination or compliance issue only when the applicable scope, governing expectation, due or milestone context, and authorized issue origin are explicitly identifiable.

Findings that do not satisfy issue-admissibility conditions shall not be reported as overdue obligations, compliance failures, or performance metrics; they shall remain observations or review feedback until governed conditions are met.
QA/QC evaluation shall first establish that the information is valid for evaluation in its current declared context, phase and purpose before testing it against compliance expectations.

Continuous monitoring, expectation-based QA/QC and milestone QA/QC shall be distinguished by purpose and consequence: continuous monitoring produces readiness signals, expectation-based QA/QC tests declared expectations, and milestone QA/QC supports governed coordination, review or release decisions at declared gates.

QA/QC findings shall have consequence only within the reviewer's governed role, review scope, information state and declared authority; findings outside those bounds shall remain observations pending appropriate governance action.

Dashboards, metrics, reports, coordination views, issue closure or coordination sign-off shall not independently create ISO 19650 approval-for-sharing, authorization or acceptance authority; they are supplementary evidence and governance mechanisms.

implementation_boundary: This L4 standard is tool-agnostic and supplementary to the ISO 19650 information-management sequence. ACC, Navisworks, folder paths, export presets, numeric project tolerances and issue-platform mechanics are implementation/project rules. S5 coordination sign-off does not replace the ISO 19650 approval-for-sharing, authorization or acceptance activities governed through S3 and S7.

provenance.migration_note: Machine-readable core reconciled with active narrative material. ISO-IMP-005 re-audit classifies S5 coordination and coordination sign-off as TIVERIT supplementary governance within collaborative information production; these controls may provide evidence to ISO reviews but do not replace ISO approval-for-sharing, authorization or acceptance decisions.
